note: Rodent antipsychotic screens (conditioned avoidance, psychostimulant hyperlocomotion) and striatal cAMP/cGMP readouts carried mardepodect, balipodect and elpipodect into schizophrenia trials; striatal occupancy was reached in people, but no member separated from placebo on its primary endpoint.
label: Schizophrenia (PDE10A)

engagement.model: Rodent striatal cAMP/cGMP and PDE10A occupancy
engagement.note: TAK-063 raised striatal cAMP and cGMP and phosphorylated PKA/PKG substrates in rodents at 0.3-1 mg/kg; no human readout yet.
engagement.quote: TAK-063 at 0.3 and 1 mg/kg p.o., increased cAMP and cGMP levels in the rodent striatum and upregulated phosphorylation levels of key substrates of cAMP- and cGMP-dependent protein kinases.

engagement.model: Rodent striatal cAMP/cGMP and PDE10A occupancy
engagement.note: Human [11C]T-773 PET: TAK-063 occupied putamen PDE10A 2.8-72% across 3-1000 mg, rising with dose and plasma level, as in rodents.
engagement.quote: PDE10A occupancy in the putamen ranged from 2.8% to 72.1% at 3hours after a single administration of 3 to 1000mg of TAK-063, and increased in a dose- and plasma concentration-dependent manner.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; healthy volunteers; the rodent readout was striatal cAMP/cGMP while the human readout is occupancy.
engagement.judgement: Paired with Suzuki 2015: the model's engagement claim was striatal PDE10A inhibition; humans showed dose-dependent striatal occupancy, the direct measure. Human cAMP/cGMP was not measured, so the model's own proximal readout is unverified. Delnomdedieu 2017 (10.1016/j.neuropharm.2017.01.016) gave 45-63% occupancy at 20 mg PF-02545920 in healthy men, the same direction for mardepodect.

engagement.note: Takeda set reversal of ketamine-induced EEG gamma and BOLD changes in rats and monkeys as the readout a healthy-volunteer study must reproduce.
engagement.short: Animal ketamine readout set as gate
engagement.quote: The main objective was to demonstrate that the effects of TAK-063 were consistent in nonclinical and clinical studies, and the decision to move into phase 2 development was contingent on consistency between phase 1 results and critical preclinical data.
engagement.confidence_note: Proxy opening year: the Go-criteria table names the rat and monkey findings before the human study began (NCT01892189, start 2013-08); the animal data were published in Tomimatsu 2016 (doi 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2016.10.006, abstract read).
engagement.judgement: Opened at the start of the human ketamine study that the animal readout gated; the readout is downstream of PDE10A, unlike the draft's striatal cAMP/cGMP track.
engagement.model: Rat and monkey ketamine-challenge phMRI/EEG reversal

engagement.note: TAK-063 reduced ketamine-induced resting BOLD effect sizes in key regions in 27 healthy men, as it had in rats and monkeys.
engagement.short: Ketamine BOLD reversal reproduced in humans
engagement.quote: Our results are consistent with non-clinical studies of ketamine and TAK-063 and clinical studies of ketamine and risperidone.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read; effect sizes rather than significance tests are reported. Registry results for NCT01892189 were posted 2017-01-12 but do not state the comparison.
engagement.reason: Human ketamine BOLD moved as in animals
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison dated to the paper's online date (2019-11-26); a pairing of Tomimatsu 2016 with the 2017 registry posting could date it to 2017. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Reduction of ketamine-induced resting-state BOLD effect size (Cohen's d)
engagement.model: Rat and monkey ketamine-challenge phMRI/EEG reversal

dose.note: Rodent MK-801 hyperlocomotion set the antipsychotic-like dose of TAK-063 at 0.3-1 mg/kg; no human exposure or occupancy target was stated.
dose.quote: TAK-063 at 0.3 and 1 mg/kg p.o., strongly suppressed MK-801 [(5R,10S)-(+)-5-methyl-10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cyclohepten-5,10-imine]-induced hyperlocomotion, which is often used as a predictive model for antipsychotic-like activity in rodents.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the quote exceeds 40 words only because of the chemical name of MK-801.
dose.judgement: Balipodect's dose track: the rodent paper states an effective mg/kg dose but no human exposure, occupancy or margin that a trial could check, so it stays untested.

dose.note: Earlier public date: Uthayathas (epub 2013-10) put the rat CAR IC50 (Cp,u 0.16 nM) beside exposures examined in the monotherapy Phase 2A; target reached, PANSS not separated.
dose.quote: In fact, mean MP-10 Cp,u 1–3 h after 0.21 and 0.67 mg/kg were approximately 0.19 nM and 0.89 nM, respectively, which were similar to those examined in the MP-10 Phase 2A study.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3934827); the preceding sentence ties the 0.16 nM Cp,u to rat conditioned avoidance. DeMartinis 2019 (10.1097/JCP.0000000000001047; NCT01939548 results 2016-08-22) later said the same for adjunctive use: PF-02545920 exposures in patients sat inside the range predicted to be efficacious, yet PANSS did not separate from placebo; the exposure target was reached and was not enough.
dose.judgement: Dated to the earliest public statement of the comparison (ruling: earliest public date). Dose table row 'target reached': same; the failure counts in efficacy. Not a retrodiction: the rodent target predates the trial. The monotherapy trial is NCT01175135 (results posted 2018-03-20).
dose.magnitude_basis: unbound plasma exposure versus rat CAR IC50 (0.16 nM)

efficacy.note: Pfizer's TP-10 and MP-10 (PF-02545920) were profiled in rodent antipsychotic screens; Pfizer proposed PDE10A as a schizophrenia target.
efficacy.quote: These new pharmacological tools enabled studies that provide further evidence that inhibition of PDE10A represents an important new target for the treatment of schizophrenia and related disorders of basal ganglia function.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not list the behavioural screens by name.

efficacy.note: Monotherapy PF-02545920 5/15 mg BID for 4 weeks in acute exacerbation missed PANSS (first public 2012-13); the adjunctive 12-week trial and every later member trial also failed.
efficacy.quote: MP-10 did not meet the primary endpoint for a reduction in psychotic symptoms in a recent Phase 2A trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01175135), although the compound was reported to cause sedation and side effects consistent with target engagement.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3934827, epub 2013-10, print 2014). The SIRS 2012 poster (10.1016/s0920-9964(12)70783-1, April 2012) is earlier but its abstract text could not be read, so it cannot carry the quote. Monotherapy registry results NCT01175135 posted 2018-03-20; Walling 2019 (10.1097/JCP.0000000000001128) is the full report.
efficacy.judgement: Moved from the adjunctive trial (DeMartinis 2019; NCT01939548 results 2016-08-22) to the monotherapy failure, public earlier (ruling: earliest public date; a congress abstract would count but the 2012 poster is unread). Uthayathas's abstract names rodent models that 'predict antipsychotic efficacy' beside the failed trial, so comparison_stated. No member trial turned the cell: balipodect (p=0.115), elpipodect 2a/2b and Lu AF11167 (futility) all missed; same result, so not split into drug tracks.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PANSS total change versus placebo at week 4

patient_trials.quote: Current data and results of a prior monotherapy study in which PF-02545920 failed to differentiate from placebo refute the hypothesis that PDE10A inhibitors have use as antipsychotic agents for schizophrenia.

The primary endpoint, change from baseline in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale total score at week 6, was not achieved (least-squares mean difference vs placebo [standard error] = -5.46 [3.44]; p = 0.115).
Lack of efficacy based on interim analysis
These findings suggest that PDE10A inhibition does not have antipsychotic effects at the doses tested.

efficacy.note: Takeda ran a ketamine challenge in healthy men to test whether TAK-063 blocks ketamine-induced brain changes and psychotic-like symptoms before phase 2.
efficacy.quote: Effects of TAK-063 on Preventing Ketamine-Induced Brain Activity Changes as Well as Psychotic-Like Symptoms in Healthy Male Adults
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record: first posted 2013-07-04, start 2013-08, completed 2014-08.
efficacy.judgement: Quote is the registry title. Run after mardepodect's monotherapy failure was public (2012 poster; 2013 paper), so this class-level model is a retrodiction; the opener stays untested.

efficacy.note: Retrodiction: the challenge ran after mardepodect had failed; it predicted benefit, and TAK-063 20 mg then missed PANSS in acute schizophrenia (p=0.115).
efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint, change from baseline in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale total score at week 6, was not achieved (least-squares mean difference vs placebo [standard error] = -5.46 [3.44]; p = 0.115).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Model side: Takeda 2020 full text (PMC7689203) records the Go decision but does not mention the phase 2 result, so this is a pairing; Yurgelun-Todd 2020 itself says predictivity was unknown.
efficacy.reason: Human challenge passed; patient trial failed
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated. Dated to the NCT02477020 results posting (2017-09-29); the challenge's own results were posted 2017-01-12. Takeda states the phase 1 results 'showed some consistent evidence of antipsychotic activity', so the model predicted benefit. Magnitude null: the drug was numerically better but not separated. Ruling (efficacy is a claim about the target): the challenge's result was first public in 2017, after mardepodect's patient failure (2012-13), so retrodiction: true; it failed to reproduce that failure, so the status stays contra.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PANSS total change vs placebo at week 6

safety.model: Rat catalepsy, prolactin and glucose vs D2 antagonists
safety.note: TAK-063 left prolactin and glucose flat and gave only weak catalepsy at 3 mg/kg, ten times the antipsychotic-like dose; authors predicted a tolerability edge.
safety.quote: At 3 mg/kg p.o., TAK-063 elicited a weak cataleptic response compared with haloperidol and olanzapine.

safety.model: Rat catalepsy, prolactin and glucose vs D2 antagonists
safety.note: TAK-063 20 mg: akathisia 11/83 vs 4/81 and dystonia 5/83 vs 1/81 on placebo; PF-02545920 15 mg dystonia 6/74 vs 3/74.
safety.short: EPS in patients at clinical dose
safety.quote: No deaths occurred, and the incidence of akathisia and dystonia, categories of extrapyramidal syndromes, was more frequent in the TAK-063 group than placebo.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; counts from the NCT02477020 and NCT01175135 registry adverse-event tables.
safety.reason: Rats predicted EPS edge; EPS appeared
safety.judgement: Call: the rat screen placed catalepsy only at ten times the antipsychotic-like dose and concluded a tolerability edge; patients had akathisia and dystonia above placebo at the dose tested, which also gave no efficacy. Dated to the NCT02477020 results posting (2017-09-29). A reader who counts the weak rat catalepsy as a correct EPS signal could score this same. Not counted in dose because the target dose was reached, not blocked.
